29.87000,-1.94000.name: Approval for Intentional introduction into the environment of Living Modified Maize
29.87000,-1.94000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-74.06880,40.96460.name: Valley Hospital Fertility Center
-74.06880,40.96460.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ali Nasseri, MD, PHD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-2.99141,56.46168.name: Ninewells Hospital
-2.99141,56.46168.state: Assisted Conception Unit, Ward 35, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee, DD1 9SY, United Kingdom
-2.99141,56.46168.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. -0.17490,51.49880.name: Target Malaria
-0.17490,51.49880.desc: A research consortium funded largely by the Gates Foundation, developing gene-drive mosquitoes intended to suppress the species that carries malaria in West Africa. It has released non-drive engineered mosquitoes in Burkina Faso as a staged step toward the real thing. Whatever one concludes, this is the most consequential deliberate release being prepared anywhere: a drive is designed to spread itself through a wild population without further releases, and nobody has demonstrated a way to recall one.

-0.17490,51.49880.name: Target Malaria — Imperial College programme record
-0.17490,51.49880.desc: The published record of the gene-drive mosquito programme: the staged releases in Burkina Faso, Ghana and Uganda, the risk assessments, and the community consent processes conducted before each step. It is the most documented approach to an engineered release anywhere, deliberately so, because a drive designed to spread through a wild population cannot be recalled and the programme knows the precedent it is setting will govern everything after it.

-0.17490,51.49880.name: Transmission Zero
-0.17490,51.49880.state: London — Imperial College, with Tanzanian and Swiss partners
-0.17490,51.49880.desc: Established in 2016 to build a two-part technology: a modification that stops a mosquito transmitting the malaria parasite, and a gene drive to carry that trait through the wild population without killing it. That second half is the distinction worth holding — most engineered mosquito programmes on this map suppress a population, and this one replaces a trait within it, which means the mosquitoes remain and the disease transmission does not. Its own stated position on pace is unusually candid: move at the right speed, not too fast, make sure people are supportive, and still treat malaria as the emergency it is. Further research, risk assessment, regulatory engagement and community consultation are all stated as preceding any field trial.

-77.04300,38.92100.name: Physicians Committee / animal testing policy
-77.04300,38.92100.desc: A US organisation campaigning against animal testing on medical rather than welfare grounds, arguing that results in animals predict human responses poorly. It was among the forces behind the FDA Modernization Act of 2022, which removed the statutory requirement for animal testing before human trials — the first change to that requirement since 1938, and one that has not yet altered practice much.

-86.01000,39.92000.name: Elanco Animal Health
-86.01000,39.92000.desc: One of the largest animal health companies in the world, spun out of Eli Lilly. It sells the medicines that make dense livestock production possible, which puts it in the same position as the edited disease-resistance work on this map — both make the conditions survivable rather than changing them, and both are sold to the same producers.

-96.77000,32.86000.name: MPEG LA / Avanci — CRISPR patent pool attempt
-96.77000,32.86000.desc: Tried to assemble a one-stop CRISPR licence covering patents held by dozens of institutions, on the model used for video codecs. It has not taken hold, which is the finding: the editing patent estate is fragmented enough that even the patent-pooling industry could not consolidate it.

-122.16900,37.42900.name: Preventive
-122.16900,37.42900.desc: One of a small number of ventures openly working toward heritable human genome editing, funded privately and stating that intention. Germline editing is prohibited in most of the world and the prohibitions are national, so a company can be lawful somewhere while its work is a crime elsewhere.

77.39100,28.53550.name: Gene Campaign
77.39100,28.53550.desc: An Indian research and advocacy organisation that brought its own petition to the Supreme Court alongside the longer-running one, seeking a halt on environmental release until a transparent biosafety protocol conducted by independent bodies was placed in the public domain. Both petitions were heard together and decided on the same day in July 2024. It belongs on this map because the crop side rarely records who actually files: a court cannot act without a petitioner, and in the country with the world's second largest population and only one commercially approved transgenic crop, the petitioners have been a small number of named individuals and organisations for twenty years.
